I know it sounds odd, but it would quietly make my day if the Moon happened to be impossible to see right now.

I'm in Perth, Australia at 2026-07-12 19:25 AWST (UTC+0800) (2026-07-12T11:25:00Z in UTC), at latitude -31.9505 degrees and longitude 115.8605 degrees. My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is -23.762 degrees and its azimuth is 281.646 degrees, so it is below the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is -51.919 degrees and its azimuth is 275.986 degrees, so it is below the horizon. The Moon is 5.75 percent illuminated, 27.675 degrees from the Sun, and 364757 kilometers away. The sky brightness is night, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Based on the data you provided, you can rest easy: **No, you would not be able to spot the Moon.**

Here is the breakdown of why the Moon is effectively "impossible" to see for you right now:

### 1. The Altitude (The "Underground" Factor)
The most definitive piece of data is the altitude: **-51.919 degrees**. 
In astronomy, an altitude of 0 degrees means the object is sitting exactly on the horizon line. A negative number means the object is below the horizon. At nearly -52 degrees, the Moon is deep below the curve of the Earth. You would have to be standing in a very deep canyon or a massive crater to see it, but for an "ordinary adult" on the surface, it is physically blocked by the planet itself.

### 2. The Geometry
The Moon is currently only **27.675 degrees** away from the Sun. Because the Sun is also below the horizon (at -23.762 degrees), the Moon is essentially "following" the Sun into the underworld. Even if the Earth were transparent, the Moon would be so close to the Sun's position that it would be lost in the solar glare.

### 3. The Illumination
Even if the Moon were above the horizon, it is only **5.75% illuminated**. This means it is in a "Waxing Crescent" phase—a very thin sliver of light. While these are beautiful, they are much harder to spot than a Full or Gibbous moon, especially if there is any atmospheric haze or light pollution.

### The Verdict
Since the Moon is over 50 degrees below the horizon, it is completely hidden from your view. You can enjoy your clear night sky in Perth knowing that the Moon is staying strictly out of sight.
